sections.heading: England's Twickenham ticket allocation still unsold as rivals sell out
sections.body: England's ticket allocation for next month's Nations Championship finale at Twickenham was increased from 1,500 to 2,000, yet seats were still available on Wednesday at £164.80 apiece — while South Africa and New Zealand have both sold out their capped 1,000-ticket 'support your team' quotas. Organisers remain bullish, with 60-65% of finals-weekend tickets sold overall, but the shortfall comes after England's last Twickenham outing, a chastening 42-21 defeat by Ireland during their worst Six Nations campaign.

sections.heading: Mark Rhydderch-Roberts reveals WRU snubbed his radical reform chairman bid

sections.heading: Argentina denied last-gasp try against England as refereeing controversy dominates headlines
sections.body: The fallout from Argentina’s 24-31 loss to England has intensified as pundits label the officiating "chaos" following a disallowed last-gasp try. A controversial TMO intervention in the final seconds denied Los Pumas a potential comeback victory in the Nations Championship Round 3 clash. The defeat leaves the side eighth in the standings with a solitary win from three starts. While the dominant five-try display against Wales earlier in the tournament offered hope, the focus now shifts to consistency before the November internationals.

sections.heading: Félix Páez Molina hails 2035 bid as vital for South American rugby
sections.body: Argentine Rugby Union president Félix Páez Molina has described the joint South American bid for the 2035 Rugby World Cup as a "very important step" for the region. Argentina are leading a four-nation consortium alongside Brazil, Chile and Uruguay, with technical information now submitted to World Rugby. The proposal includes 11 venues, such as the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires and the Maracanã in Rio de Janeiro. This first-ever South American bid faces competition from Spain, Italy and Japan, with a final decision expected in November 2027.

lead.why: UAR president Félix Páez Molina provided fresh comments on the bid's potential impact on the region.
